findings.note: The implementation report states a measurement of the shipped bytes that the shipped bytes contradict, and contradicts itself inside one bullet. It says 'At the shipped bytes, grep -c ^def run_t007_ reports sixteen'; running exactly that pattern over the test driver the bundle carries yields SEVENTEEN (bundle lines 34814, 34895, 35105, 35250, 35346, 35424, 35520, 35597, 35674, 35737, 35819, 35904, 36020, 36122, 36238, 36339, 36553), and all seventeen are dispatched from main. The same bullet says 'seventeen run_t007_* functions' nine lines earlier and 'the current value is fifteen' three lines later, so three different values for one countable fact sit in one paragraph. The same bullet also says 'eleven new fixture directories' while the next section says 'Thirteen fixture scenario directories'; thirteen is correct against the declared-output sections. A reader cannot determine the shipped state from the record, and the false figure is framed as a direct grep result rather than as prose. This is the sibling-description drift class this package has already remediated repeatedly.

findings.note: The shipped, user-facing CHANGELOG entry carries two counts that are wrong at these bytes. Line 24558 states the task owns eleven fixture scenario directories; the declared outputs and the driver's own case_name set both give thirteen (artifact-publication-failed, clean-full-track-publication, post-publication-crash-before-evidence, post-publication-generation-mismatch, publication-fsync-failure, publication-journal-recovery, publication-journal-recovery-crash, publication-journal-roundtrip-unresolved-repo, publication-journal-target-escape, publication-staging-chain-fsync-failure, publication-staging-parent-symlink, publication-target-parent-symlink, snapshot-generation-mismatch-affected-components). Line 24591 states '15 mutant, 13 covered'; mutation-proofs.log carries sixteen mutants A through P with fourteen killed. The entry's own mutation enumeration also never mentions the staging-chain durability barrier mutant. The uncovered pair (F and O) is stated correctly, so only the totals drifted, but both are quantitative claims about the shipped state in a declared output and both are false.

The impossibility argument disclosed for mutant O is refuted by this same log's precedent for mutant M. The note says 'no in-process injection can make the DIFFERENCE visible, because the end state is identical on every non-crashing path' - but the mutant M note two entries earlier concedes that the overlay makes the fsync CALL observable even when its durability effect is not. The unlink-side barrier is reached on existing fixtures: the Context Projection target is ABSENT at PRE on a first publish, so the rollback takes the unlink-plus-fsync branch and fsyncs the generated directory. An overlay armed on that directory would raise, driving the shipped code into the incomplete-rollback clause with the journal retained, while mutant O (barrier removed) would report a completed rollback - an observable difference in stderr and in journal survival. This is the fourth unreachability claim of this shape in this task; the previous three (C, D, M) were each shown wrong by a panelist. The coverage state itself is honestly labelled UNCOVERED, so nothing is overclaimed; only the reason given is unsound.

The staging-chain overlay installs _tracking_replace and populates _renamed, but _failing_fsync gates only on 'fd in _feature_dir_fds and not _fired' and never consults _renamed - unlike the sibling publication-fsync-failure overlay, where _renamed is what arms the injection. The arming machinery is dead here, and the comment copied along with it ('Arm only once a rename has actually landed in the feature directory ... The arm makes the fixture mean what its name says') describes behaviour this fixture does not have and must not have, since its whole point is to fire on the pre-rename barrier. The assertions are still correct and mutant P dies against them; the residue is a misleading comment plus unused monkeypatching of os.replace inside a fault-injection fixture.
